claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 in the target state has a hierarchical heterostructure containing multilevel chemical fluctuations and phase boundaries.
A physics-informed reduced-order machine-learning model can predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Multiscale chemical fluctuations and phase boundaries govern local deformation in hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Multiscale chemical fluctuations and phase boundaries govern damage initiation and propagation in hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Embedding simplified micromechanics in the machine-learning model can capture the critical effects of local phase distribution.
Embedding simplified micromechanics in the machine-learning model can capture the critical effects of damage evolution.
Reduced experimental feature sets representing micromechanical signatures can be correlated with global mechanical properties.
The reduced-order model can bypass the need for full-scale high-fidelity simulations.
The proposed model will reduce computational time by more than one order of magnitude relative to full high-fidelity simulations.
The proposed model will predict Young’s modulus within 5–10% of benchmark experimental measurements.
The proposed model will predict yield strength within 5–10% of benchmark experimental measurements.
The proposed model will predict fracture toughness within 10–15% of benchmark experimental measurements.
The model’s reliability will diminish at high strain rates outside its calibrated quasi-static regime.
The model’s reliability will diminish at extreme temperatures outside its room-temperature calibration regime.
The model’s reliability will diminish when microstructural evolution falls outside the calibration parameter space.
